topics.title: Mid-Term Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to
- Rest and prepare for the second half of the term
- Reflect on what they have learned so far

Introduction:
This week is a break from regular classes to allow students to rest and recharge. The mid-term break gives everyone time to recover from the first part of the term.

Content:
During the mid-term break, students should take time to review what they have learned about computer hardware and GSM repairs. They can practice identifying different computer components and mobile phone parts. Students might visit computer repair shops in their local markets to observe real technicians at work. This break is also a good time to organize your notes and repair tools for when classes resume.

Class activity:
Students should spend time observing computer or mobile phone repair activities in their community. They can draw diagrams of common computer parts or mobile phone components they see.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the purpose of the mid-term break?
2. Name three computer components you have learned about so far.
3. How can you use your break time to improve your understanding of GSM repairs?

Summary:
The mid-term break is an important time for rest and reflection on what you have learned about computer hardware and GSM repairs.

topics.title: Rights and Duties of Citizens
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list consumer protection laws relevant to computer hardware and GSM repairs.
The students should be able to explain the importance of integrity in customer service.
The students should be able to identify accountability measures in a repair business.

Introduction:
Today we will discuss the rights and duties of citizens in the context of computer hardware and GSM repairs. This builds on our previous lessons about repair techniques and business management.

Content:
Consumer protection laws are rules that protect customers from unfair business practices. In Nigeria, these include the Consumer Protection Council Act which ensures fair pricing and quality service. For example, if a customer pays for a phone screen replacement, the repairer must use quality parts not substandard ones. Integrity means being honest and ethical in all business dealings. A repairer with integrity will explain all charges clearly and not add hidden costs. Accountability means taking responsibility for your actions. If a repair causes further damage, an accountable technician will fix it without extra charge. In Nigerian markets like Computer Village in Lagos, customers expect repairers to be accountable for their work.

Class activity:
Students will role-play a scenario where a customer brings a faulty phone to their repair shop. They must demonstrate proper consumer protection practices including explaining the problem clearly, stating the price upfront, and explaining their warranty policy.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the purpose of consumer protection laws in Nigeria?
2. How can a repair technician demonstrate integrity in their business?
3. Why is accountability important in the GSM repair business?
4. Give an example of unethical behavior a repairer might show towards customers.

Summary:
Understanding rights and duties helps create trust between repairers and customers, leading to better business practices and customer satisfaction.

topics.title: Practical: Setting up a Mini GSM Shop
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to design a business plan for a small GSM repair shop.
The students should be able to create a functional layout for a mini GSM shop.
The students should be able to identify necessary equipment for a GSM repair business.

Introduction:
Building on our previous lessons about GSM repairs, today we will learn how to set up a mini GSM shop. This practical skill will help you understand what it takes to run a successful repair business.

Content:
A business plan is a document that outlines your business goals and how you will achieve them. For a mini GSM shop, your plan should include services offered (phone repairs, unlocking, accessories), pricing strategy, and target customers. The shop layout should be organized with separate areas for customer service, repair work, and sales of accessories. Essential equipment includes screwdriver sets, soldering irons, testing machines, and spare parts storage. In Nigeria, many successful GSM shops start small in market stalls like those in Onitsha Main Market before expanding. Your shop should have good lighting and proper ventilation as you will be working with small electronic parts. Customer service area should be welcoming with seating for waiting customers.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create a detailed business plan and layout diagram for a mini GSM shop. They will include equipment lists, pricing for common repairs, and a floor plan showing different functional areas.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three essential pieces of equipment needed for a GSM repair shop?
2. Why is a good shop layout important for customer satisfaction?
3. List two services that could be offered in a mini GSM shop.
4. How might pricing strategy affect the success of a small GSM business in Nigeria?

Summary:
Setting up a mini GSM shop requires careful planning of both business operations and physical space to create an efficient and customer-friendly environment.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify the main components of a computer system.
The students should be able to list common GSM faults and their possible solutions.
The students should be able to explain the basic steps in troubleshooting computer hardware problems.
The students should be able to demonstrate how to perform basic GSM software troubleshooting.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we have learned this term about computer hardware and GSM repairs. This revision will help you remember important concepts we covered and prepare you for your final examination.

Content:
Computer hardware refers to the physical parts of a computer that you can see and touch. The main components include the central processing unit (CPU), which is the brain of the computer; the random access memory (RAM), which temporarily stores data while the computer is on; the hard disk drive (HDD) or solid state drive (SSD), which stores data permanently; and the motherboard, which connects all components together. Other components include the power supply unit, graphics processing unit (GPU), and input/output devices like keyboards and monitors. In Nigeria, common computer brands include HP, Dell, and Innjoo, which are popular in offices and cybercafés across the country.

GSM repairs involve fixing issues with mobile phones and communication devices. Common GSM faults include charging problems, which could be due to faulty chargers, damaged charging ports, or bad batteries; network issues, which might result from poor SIM card contact, software problems, or hardware defects; and screen problems, such as cracks or unresponsive touchscreens. GSM repair technicians in Nigeria often work in small shops in markets like Computer Village in Lagos, where they fix phones using tools like screwdrivers, soldering irons, and software flashing devices. Harmattan season can also affect phone performance due to dust and dry air, so proper maintenance is important.

Troubleshooting computer hardware problems follows a systematic approach. First, identify the problem by asking questions and observing symptoms. Second, make a hypothesis about the cause. Third, test your hypothesis by checking connections, replacing components, or using diagnostic tools. Fourth, implement the solution. For example, if a computer won't turn on, check the power cable, power strip, and finally the power supply unit. In Nigerian classrooms, computers often face power issues due to unstable electricity supply, so surge protectors and voltage stabilizers are essential equipment.

Class activity:
Divide the class into four groups. Each group will be given a scenario describing a computer or GSM problem. They will discuss and write down the steps to troubleshoot and solve the problem. One group will handle a computer that won't boot, another a phone that won't charge, another a computer with no display, and the last a phone with network issues. Each group will present their solution to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. List four main components of a computer system and explain their functions.
2. What are three common GSM faults and their possible causes?
3. Describe the steps in troubleshooting a computer that shows no power when you press the power button.
4. How would you troubleshoot a GSM phone that cannot make or receive calls?
5. Why is it important to follow a systematic approach when repairing electronic devices?

Summary:
Today's revision covered the essential components of computer hardware, common GSM faults and repairs, and systematic troubleshooting methods to solve technical problems effectively.

topics.title: Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different computer hardware components.
The students should be able to explain basic GSM troubleshooting steps.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper handling of computer and GSM tools.

Introduction:
Today we will be conducting your end-of-term examination covering all the topics we have studied this term. This test will help me know how well you have understood the computer hardware and GSM repairs we have been learning about.

Content:
The examination will cover the following topics:
1. Introduction to Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs - You should be able to define what computer hardware is, name different types of computers, and explain what GSM repairs involve. Remember that computer hardware includes physical components like the CPU, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and motherboard. GSM repairs involve fixing mobile phones and their accessories.
2. Classification of computers - You should be able to list and explain different types of computers such as desktops, laptops, tablets, and servers. You should also be able to give examples of how each type is used in Nigeria, like how a danfo conductor might use a smartphone for payments, or how a market trader uses a simple calculator.
3. Basic components of a computer system - You should be able to identify and explain the function of the main components including the CPU, RAM, hard drive, motherboard, and power supply. Think of the CPU as the brain of the computer, just like your head controls your body.
4. Introduction to GSM technology - You should be able to explain what GSM stands for (Global System for Mobile Communications) and describe how it works in Nigeria. Remember how we use our phones to make calls, send messages, and browse the internet even during harmattan season when network might be poor.
5. Common computer and GSM problems - You should be able to identify common issues like computers not turning on, phones not charging, and screens not displaying properly. For example, when a kerosene stove has problems, we check the fuel and the lighter; similarly, when phones have problems, we check the battery and charger.
6. Basic troubleshooting steps - You should be able to list and explain steps to fix common problems. This includes checking connections, restarting devices, and using appropriate tools. Always remember to turn off the power before opening any device to avoid damage.

Class activity:
After completing your examination papers, you will work in groups of four to identify different computer hardware components and GSM parts using pictures. Each group will list the components they can identify and explain their functions.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three types of computer hardware and explain their functions.
2. What does GSM stand for and what is its main purpose?
3. Describe two common problems that can occur with mobile phones and how to troubleshoot them.
4. Why is it important to turn off power before opening a computer or phone for repair?
5. How would you explain the function of a CPU to someone who has never seen a computer before?

Summary:
Today's examination has tested your knowledge of computer hardware and GSM repairs, which are essential skills in our increasingly digital world.

topics.title: Closing / Vacation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall the main topics covered in the term.
The students should be able to explain the importance of computer hardware and GSM repair skills in today's digital world.
The students should be able to list three career opportunities in computer hardware and GSM repairs.

Introduction:
This week marks the end of the term and we will be reviewing what we have learned about computer hardware and GSM repairs. This knowledge will be useful during the vacation period and in your future studies.

Content:
Throughout this term, we have explored various aspects of computer hardware and GSM repairs. We started with the basic components of a computer system including the CPU, motherboard, RAM, and storage devices. We learned how to identify these components and understand their functions. We also studied common hardware problems and their solutions, such as troubleshooting a computer that won't power on or fixing a faulty keyboard.

In the GSM repair section, we examined the different parts of a mobile phone, including the screen, battery, charging port, and motherboard. We practiced basic repair techniques like screen replacement and battery installation. We also discussed safety precautions when handling electronic devices, such as disconnecting power sources before opening any device and using anti-static wristbands to prevent damage from static electricity.

We learned about the history of computers and GSM technology in Nigeria, which has evolved significantly over the years. From the large mainframe computers to the smartphones we use today, technology has transformed how we communicate and work in Nigeria. We also discussed the classification of computers based on size and purpose, from supercomputers to microcomputers like our personal computers and smartphones.

Class activity:
Prepare a short presentation on one topic you found most interesting this term. You can choose to demonstrate a simple repair technique, explain a computer component, or discuss how GSM technology has changed communication in Nigeria. Your presentation should be 3-5 minutes long and include visual aids if possible.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three components of a computer system and explain their functions.
2. What safety precautions should you take when repairing a GSM device?
3. How has GSM technology changed communication in Nigeria?
4. Describe one common computer hardware problem and its solution.
5. Why are computer hardware and GSM repair skills important in today's job market?

Summary:
This term has provided you with valuable knowledge and skills in computer hardware and GSM repairs that you can continue to develop during the vacation period.
